newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks set new record highs.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks set new record highs.

text.p: Madrid's general index closed at a new record high on Monday, with dealers optmistic ahead of CPI data and labour reform talks later this week.
However, dealers could not rule out the possibility of profit taking in the short run.
The general index rose 8.72 points, 1.81 percent, to 489.60 points, while the Ibex-35 closed 117 points, 2.14 percent, higher at 5,620.74.
"Shares are very strong and we have the feeling that a good February CPI and a deal on labour reforms could boost the market," a dealer in Madrid said.
February CPI data, due on Thursday, is expected to show a new record low, while on Wednesday trade unions and employers will meet again in an effort to reach an agreement over labour market reform.
Share market volume was high, with 94 billion pesetas changing hands. Telefonica ended 50 pesetas higher to 3,490 pesetas, while Repsol gained 40 pesetas to 5,850 pesetas.
